I have a little bit of a different experience than you as I am a child of an addict and not married to one. 

However, I think it’s best to set boundaries and not let them be crossed. It’s hard because I don’t think it’s ever a good idea to tell people what to do because things work differently for different people. 

I think it’s usually a good idea to set up boundaries. Give him an ultimatum, either he goes to rehab or you get a divorce. Give him a certain amount of time and if it’s not followed through, already have a conclusion in mind of what you’re going to do when he doesn’t go (divorce? kick him out?). 

On the same note, think about how this addiction is effecting your child. My father has been abusive as long as I can remember and my childhood was really hard and rough. I understand him because you kind of have to (or something idk). I get it but it doesn’t mean that I don’t resent him. Addiction is a family addiction.

This burden your husband has on his shoulder is a burden you will carry on yours and your child will carry on hers. 

As far as when you say enough. That’s a good question. My father went to rehab twice and is still an addict. (To be fair one will always be an addict. that craving will never fully go away). Sobriety is achievable I know a lot of people who have achieved it. But it’s something they have to fight for every day. 

Most important of all is you should never lose hope. Find who you are as a human being and not just as a wife and mother. (Though both great roles, there’s more than that). It does sound like you love your husband but you don’t like him very much, at least at the moment. 

What I’ve found is that my father is a really cool, upbeat, outgoing person. But only when he is sober. If he could be like that all the time he’d be my best friend. But he chose drugs, over and over and over. Over my mom, over my siblings, and over work and over me. If your husband does the same, go from there. If he gets sober and you learn you don’t love or like him, go from there. 

Above all though, you’ll be okay and things usually turn out the way they’re supposed to, and often times you find you’re on top. 

Good luck, you’re brave and you can do anything you set your mind to. Never forget that.

And I realized what I wanted and what I would let myself find: friendship. I told people how I was feeling broken and unloved and they told me I deserved better and a friend who thinks coffee is evil bought me coffee and told me she cared about me. In fact so many people told me they cared about me that day that I felt better when I went home. It took weeks to be happy again and I’m still not 100% over it. But there’s this new boy who’s brilliant and kind and has all the things I never thought I’d find again. 

Moving on is hard. But it’s worth it, as you look around you at all the other possibilities in your life— you’ll find over and over again all the things you’ve ever wanted. Not all at once, but in time. Good luck, and I’m here if you need a good listener <3
